subject: RFI: Practical SLO validation recipes and crediting steps for procurement
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <e.ruiz@acuityhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@acuityhealth.com, Danielle Park <dpark@acuityhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI — measurement approach for uptime/latency and service crediting

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this RFI. As part of our procurement checklist we need clear, machine-checkable definitions and evidence expectations for the availability and latency SLOs you propose. Please provide concise answers to the items below (we'll use the responses to validate contract language and the evidence pack):

1) Canonical uptime definition: exactly which endpoints and signals you consider for the availability window (control plane, inference endpoints, streaming endpoints).
2) Measurement window and aggregation: rolling vs calendar window, minimum sample size to compute p99/p50, and how you handle partial-region degradations.
3) Sampling vs probe types: difference between synthetic probes and production-customer-traffic measurements; how you weight or combine them.
4) Credit calculation: formula for service credits when SLOs are missed (examples for 99.9% and 99.95% across multi-region deployments).
5) Evidence artifacts: what logs/traces/metrics you will hand over for an audit (time-series CSV, raw probe responses, trace IDs, config snapshots).
6) Latency buckets and retry/backoff normalization: how retries by SDKs or client-side batching affect observed latency percentiles.
7) Dispute resolution hygiene: claim windows, retention policy for primary telemetry, and attestation headers.

We'd like a written response and an example evidence bundle for a past non-sensitive degradation (anonymized) to verify packaging. Please copy Karthik from engineering if you need technical clarifications. Can you respond by EOD Friday PST?

Appreciate it,
Elena
Procurement, Acuity Health

--
Acuity Health | procurement@acuityhealth.com
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <e.ruiz@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI — measurement approach for uptime/latency and service crediting

Elena —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Quick note up front: we will separate control-plane observability (API management, auth, config propagation) from inference-plane (model endpoints/streams) in both definitions and evidence packages — that makes attribution and crediting deterministic. Below are concise responses; I attached a short "recipes" PDF with worked examples and an evidence-pack sample as a ZIP.

1) Canonical uptime definition:
- Inference availability = successful 200-like responses from the customer-specific inference route(s) that the customer pins in their config. For streaming flows we require successful stream negotiation + first-data frame within 3s (configurable). Control-plane downtime (auth, register, model-pull) is tracked separately and is not included in inference availability percent calculations unless it causally prevents inference for > 5 minutes across all nodes.

2) Measurement window and aggregation:
- Rolling 30-day window is primary for crediting. We also report rolling 7-day and calendar-month for visibility. Percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) are computed on aggregated per-request measurements with a minimum sample floor: 10k successful requests per window per region for p99 to be considered statistically meaningful; otherwise we fallback to a hybrid synthetic weighting (see #3). Partial-region degradations: we attribute per-region; global crediting uses traffic-weighted aggregation across regions using a 30-day traffic fraction map.

3) Sampling vs probes:
- Production telemetry (server-side request logs and client request traces) is primary when sample sizes meet the floor. Synthetic probes run at 1m cadence per region and are used to fill low-traffic gaps and detect split-brain/failover. For evidence, we provide both types and publish the exact weighting used when production samples are below the floor.

4) Credit calculation (summary):
- Credit formula is: Credit% = min(100, max(0, (SLA_Target - Observed_Availability) / (1 - SLA_Target) * 100)) rounded to nearest 0.1%. We include region weighting and caps for transient spikes (events < 5 minutes per-region are excluded unless sustained). The PDF includes worked examples for 99.9% and 99.95% across 2-region and 3-region deployments.

5) Evidence artifacts:
- Time-series CSVs (per-minute availability and latency), raw probe logs (timestamp, probe-id, region, rtt, response-code), sample request traces (trace-id, span list, timestamps), config snapshot (model id, pinned version, routing policy), and a signed attestation CSV (hashes + signer key). We retain primary telemetry for 90 days by default and can extend under contract.

6) Latency buckets & retry normalization:
- We canonicalize latency as server-side first-byte-to-last-byte when available. Client-side retries are de-duplicated via request-id where present; absent dedupe falls back to server trace heuristics. We publish both raw percentiles and a retry-normalized percentile.

7) Dispute resolution:
- Claims must be filed within 30 days of the incident window close. We provide an evidence binder and a 10-business-day validation timeline. Primary telemetry retention is 90 days; archived audit copies are kept for 1 year for enterprise contracts.

I've attached the "Redwood_SLO_Measurement_Recipes.pdf" with examples and a redacted Acuity evidence sample ZIP. Karthik will add a short technical appendix on probe placement and sampling if you'd like more depth. If the high-level answers above look good we can follow up with a brief call (30 minutes) to walk the Acuity engineering team through the evidence package.

Deliverables attached: Redwood_SLO_Measurement_Recipes.pdf (summary + worked examples), Acuity_Evidence_Sample.zip (redacted CSVs + traces).

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Elena Ruiz <e.ruiz@acuityhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@acuityhealth.com, Danielle Park <dpark@acuityhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI — measurement approach for uptime/latency and service crediting

Thanks Lauren — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our engineering team (short bullets):
- When you say "traffic-weighted aggregation": what baseline period do you use to compute region weights? Can we lock that to a contract epoch?
- For the sample floor (10k requests), will you compute p99 using reservoir sampling if the window slightly undershoots the floor?
- Can you provide one concrete CSV example that shows the credit calculation performed end-to-end (observed availability numbers, traffic weights, final credit percent)?

Also, we need the evidence bundle to include the SHA256 sums for each artifact and a brief readme that lists the tool commands you used to extract data (so our auditors can reproduce). If you can get those items to us by EOD tomorrow PST, we can move forward to the redlining step.

Elena

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <e.ruiz@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI — measurement approach for uptime/latency and service crediting

Elena — quick delivery of the additional items you requested. Attached: an annotated CSV that walks an example end-to-end calculation (Acuity_demo_credit_calc.csv in the ZIP), SHA256 sums for every artifact, and a README.txt with the extraction commands and the query IDs used on our telemetry stack. Key clarifications below:

- Region weighting baseline: we default to the prior 90-day rolling traffic distribution to compute weights. Under contract we can lock a "contract epoch" (e.g., Q1 baseline) to fix weights for the term.
- Undershoot handling: when samples fall between 5k-10k we run a hybrid approach: reservoir sampling + synthetic-probe weighting; the hybrid coefficient is published in the README and is deterministic given the sample counts (see CSV). Below 5k we rely primarily on probes with an explicit dilution factor.
- End-to-end example: the CSV in the ZIP has columns: region, total_successful_requests, observed_availability, baseline_weight, weighted_availability, global_observed_availability, SLA_target, calculated_credit_percent. The worked example shows a 99.95% target being missed in one region leading to a 3.2% credit (example numbers are redacted to avoid sharing customer data).

We also included a short appendix where Karthik explains probe placement (edge vs regional aggregator) and the exact query used to compute p99 in our TSDB. If Acuity wants additional queries or raw trace attachments we can provide them under an NDA/secure transfer.

If these items look good we'll schedule a 30-minute technical review next week — I'm free Mon/Tue mornings PST.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren — thanks for the fast turnaround and the packaged evidence. Confirming receipt of the ZIP and the README; the auditors will validate the SHA sums tomorrow. If you can share a short redline we can loop our legal and get to term.

Danielle
Procurement, Acuity Health
